subject: Using an observed variable to predict mean differences between two latent variables.

messages.author: 33a49924fb977234
messages.subject: Using an observed variable to predict mean differences between two latent variables.
parts:
Hello, I have a project where I would be interested in evaluating if the latent means of two factors can be predicted by an observed variable. Let’s say the two latent variables are attitude towards the color blue and attitude towards the color red.

I want to see if age, an observed variable can predict the differences in attitude towards blue and red. How would I specify this in lavaan without using a multi group analysis and specifying one group for each value of age?

messages.subject: Re: Using an observed variable to predict mean differences between two latent variables.
parts: I want to see if age, an observed variable can predict the differences in attitude towards blue and red

The means of the blue and red factors are only comparable if their scales are linked.  Assuming their indicators are parallel (so first indicator of blue is essentially the same as the first indicator of red), then you can test measurement invariance across the constructs.  This is the same method used when measuring the same construct on multiple occasions (longitudinal invariance), but it can apply to any dependent/repeated measures (e.g., mother and father factors for responses about the same child).

If scalar ("strong") invariance holds, then you can identify the model by fixing the first factor (e.g., blue) mean to zero but freely estimate the other factor (e.g., red) mean.  Thus, the red mean would already be the mean difference between blue and red.  And you can use age as a predictor of red to obtain any moderating effect on the red mean (and thus the mean difference you are interested in).  Even though the blue mean is fixed to zero, you can estimate the age effect on that too.  In this case, to make sure the red mean remains the marginal mean difference between factors, you should mean-center age.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
